deepdive.sec: Media & Entertainment / Content IP Library Monetisation — traditional-to-digital pivot

bull_bear.body:
- **Debt ₹311cr against inventory ₹348cr.** A debt-reduction plan exists for FY27; management refused to size it, citing geopolitical uncertainty and the BARC blackout — "it's no point that I give you a target or a number right now and then it doesn't hold by the end of the year."
- Capital is being **reallocated from traditional to digital across every dimension** — money, people, AI work, content creation.
- Explicit growth-versus-burn discipline on ShemarooMe: "it's very easy for me to scale up by burning significantly more amount of money… but then that will burn a big hole on our cash flow and balance sheet… few quarters later we would ourselves scratch our heads."
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
1. **BARC ratings blackout** — began ~a month before the call, hits traditional ad monetisation directly and TV-linked syndication indirectly. No visibility on resolution. Compounds an already subdued ad market.
2. **Digital revenue is lumpy** — a 17% decline driven by deferred B2B syndication. Deferrals are recoverable in principle, but the timing is not in Shemaroo's control.
3. **Debt at ₹311cr with ~₹30cr+ of annual interest** against a business at roughly break-even EBITDA — the reduction plan is unquantified.
4. **Traditional TV is structurally declining** and some FTA channels are below break-even; channel rationalisation is possible but unconfirmed.
5. **ShemarooMe is ~2 years from profitability** and completely undisclosed — no revenue, subscribers, ARPU, DAU/MAU. An analyst explicitly requested more granularity; management committed only to discuss it offline.
6. **YouTube Shorts monetisation has not moved**, and an expected July policy update had not landed. Micro-drama monetisation is likewise unresolved.
7. **FAST is globally de-growing** — Shemaroo has already cut from more channels to two.
8. **Digital growth has been only 9–10% CAGR FY24→FY26**, below the +20% an analyst argued should be achievable; management's defence is industry growth was itself low and that it will not buy growth at the cost of cash.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Measured, technically candid, and unusually willing to correct analysts' mental models — the CEO and COO both pushed back on the assumption that YouTube is inherently the highest-margin channel, explaining that margin follows **content vintage**, not platform. They also volunteered that FAST is de-growing globally and that Shorts/micro-drama monetisation remains unproven, rather than riding the narrative. The commitments they did make were specific and falsifiable (EBITDA-positive this year, bottom-line positive next year, >50% cut in traditional new-initiative spend). The weakness is disclosure: an analyst told them directly that "there are too many things which are not disclosed and hence very difficult to figure out… how the business is moving," and the honest answer was a commitment to discuss offline. The refusal to size the debt-reduction plan is defensible given the BARC blackout, but it leaves the balance-sheet trajectory unmodellable.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The margin driver is content vintage, not platform.** Fully charged-off legacy content yields **80–90%** margins on any platform; newly acquired content can be zero or negative because acquisition is competitively priced. This single insight reframes the whole P&L — Shemaroo's earnings power is a function of how hard it mines the paid-for library relative to how much new content it buys.
- **Views are the wrong YouTube metric.** Total views are flat/range-bound and management is deliberately steering to **connected TV long-form**, which monetises far better per view. "Finally, your revenue per view or monetisation metrics are far more important."
- **The ₹18cr ex-initiative EBITDA is the real run-rate signal** — the reported −₹2cr is masked by ₹20cr of deliberate, and now shrinking (on the traditional side), investment.
- **The two-year ShemarooMe subscription plan is a genuinely unusual asset** — no other Indian platform offers one. It is prepaid duration and a trust signal in a category where churn is the killer.
- **The negative-margin history was an accounting programme, not operations.** With charge-off normalised and inventory at ₹348cr, prior-period margins are not a valid base for forecasting.
- **Micro-drama and Shorts are being held deliberately**: the tech is ready, the content isn't bought. This is a real, low-cost option that gets exercised only when monetisation proves out.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:

- Working capital release rather than fresh capex is funding the business: inventories and trade receivables fell from INR 6,823 Mn and INR 1,453 Mn in FY24 to INR 3,391 Mn and INR 694 Mn in FY26, with capital work-in-progress nil throughout.

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Structural decline of traditional television/broadcasting — Television revenues are under sustained structural pressure as advertising budgets and high-value households migrate to digital and Connected TV; industry-wide, Pay TV lost 11.5 million households in 2025 and linear TV advertising revenue declined. This directly bears on Shemaroo's Traditional segment (TV syndication, DTH, broadcasting channels), which industry-wide revenue is projected to keep declining through 2028.
- Free-to-air ecosystem changes impacting broadcasting economics — Management explicitly flagged that the broadcasting business 'operated in a challenging environment during the year as changes within the free-to-air ecosystem impacted industry economics', requiring a channel-portfolio realignment (e.g., relaunch of Chumbak TV as Shemaroo Josh).
- OTT platform spend rationalisation reducing content demand — Industry-wide, there was 'a noticeable reduction in high-budget direct-to-OTT film acquisitions as platforms rationalised spends to align with profitability targets', causing a brief dip in aggregate OTT content investment — a demand risk for Shemaroo's content licensing business, which depends on platforms continuing to acquire/license third-party content.
- Regulatory/policy risk in adjacent media segments — The M&E industry showed exposure to abrupt regulatory action — e.g., a four-month ban on real-money gaming starting August 2025 sharply stifled gaming subscriptions industry-wide — illustrating the kind of policy risk that can also affect broadcasting or content-licensing economics with little notice.
- Deteriorating leverage and coverage metrics from operating losses — The Company's own ratio commentary attributes a decrease in Interest Coverage Ratio and an increase in Debt-Equity Ratio to 'loss incurred in current year', alongside a decrease in Current Ratio linked to lower trade receivables — signalling balance-sheet strain from continued operating losses.
- No dedicated Risk Management Committee — Constitution of a Risk Management Committee under Regulation 21 of the SEBI Listing Regulations 'was not applicable to the Company during the financial year 2025-26'; risk assessment and mitigation instead rests with the Audit Committee and Board, a narrower oversight structure than peers with a dedicated RMC.
- Macro and geopolitical headwinds — The Company's cautionary statement flags dependence on 'global and national economic conditions ... business risk, changes in the Government's rules and regulations'; the MD&A separately cites the ongoing Russia-Ukraine and Israel-Hamas conflicts and broad-based US tariffs as headwinds to global trade volumes and business confidence.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- **Digital (₹56cr, −17%)** splits into a **lumpy B2B syndication/licensing leg** (the decline) and a **growing consumer leg** (fresh content, stronger engagement, improved ad monetisation). Management insists there is **no under-utilisation of the library** — 9bn views a quarter is the proof — and that titles like *Welcome*, *Jab We Met*, *Phir Hera Pheri* are consistent performers wherever placed.
- **Traditional (₹76cr, +5%)**: FTA/free-dish channels are **100% advertising-monetised**; some channels are not at break-even because the ad market has been persistently subdued. Investment here is being "pared down significantly," with possible channel rationalisation not ruled out ("whether it is in terms of channel scale rationalization or whatever, that will come to know as we go ahead").
- **ShemarooMe (SVoD, Gujarati-led)**: described as holding a "pole position" and effectively the **default Gujarati entertainment platform**. Uniquely offers a **two-year subscription plan** with decent uptake — management reads this as a trust signal, since consumers pay two years ahead without content visibility. **No numbers disclosed** — the COO would say only "strong double-digit revenue growth trajectory."
- **FAST channels**: the global FAST ecosystem has been **de-growing for 12–18 months**; Shemaroo has cut back from more channels to **two**, and treats it as experimental — "if it scales, we will scale up… if it doesn't scale, we will scale back."
- **Connected TV** is the stated strategic focus within YouTube — long-form content on CTV monetises significantly better than views elsewhere, and management says YouTube itself is focusing there.

latest_quarter.body:
- Margin is explicitly **not a linear function of revenue**. Three drivers: (i) **mix** — mine more of the already-charged-off legacy library, which carries the highest incremental EBITDA; (ii) **cost** — a significant operational-efficiency drive over the last 2–3 quarters, whose effect should show quarter-on-quarter; (iii) **value-chain position** — consumer-facing OTT makes no money for anyone today; aggregation/licensing of owned content is the profitable middle; content creation/production-for-hire is a fixed **10–20%** margin business.
- **Blended digital margin depends on legacy vs newly-acquired mix**, not on the platform (YouTube vs syndication) — management corrected an analyst who assumed YouTube was structurally the highest-margin channel.

(b) The **BARC ratings blackout** began roughly a month before the call and hits traditional TV monetisation and, secondarily, TV-linked syndication. (c) New-initiative spend on the **traditional** side is being cut by **>50% in FY27 vs FY26**, with investment redirected to digital.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue growth: "healthy double-digit" blended, over the next 2–3 years** — built as digital growing at a low-double-digit industry rate **plus at least a couple of percentage points** of outperformance, with **traditional flat (explicitly "not a degrowth")**.
- **Profitability: "the aim will be for the year to be EBITDA positive at least"** and **"we are very confident that next year we will be bottom-line positive also."** Quarter-on-quarter improvement expected every quarter.
- **Margin: "upwards of 20% EBITDA is something that we should aim for"** on a 2–3 year view (aspiration, hedged — "I don't know whether we will be able to achieve that or not").
- **Debt: a reduction plan exists for this year**, but **no quantum given** — explicitly withheld because of geopolitical uncertainty and the BARC blackout. Expect quarterly ups and downs.
- **New-initiative spend on traditional media: >50% reduction in FY27 vs FY26 — "we are well on track."**
- **H2 expected to be materially stronger** — festive season, operational gains, and the digital consumption engine.
- **Advertising outlook for traditional business: expected to remain subdued in the near term** (BARC blackout + macro + geopolitics).
- **ShemarooMe path to profitability: "at least about two years away"** — dependent on building a large permanent subscriber base and minimising churn.
- **No further inventory write-down risk** — "now we are in a normal charge-off cycle."
- Explicitly **declined**: any ShemarooMe revenue/subscriber/DAU/MAU/ARPU disclosure; a revenue threshold for sustained positive EBITDA; a segment revenue split target for FY27 beyond the directional double-digit/flat framing.
order book & pipeline:
Not an order-book business; content and distribution deals are the equivalent.
- **OHO Gujarati catalogue acquired (April 2026)** — adds **22+ Gujarati original web series** to ShemarooMe.
- **10 new titles released in the quarter** across movies, web series and plays — including the original web series *Kajodu* and the world digital premiere of *Jalebi Rocks*; also *Vitthal Teedi* S1, *Kadak Meethi* S1 & S2, *Cutting* S1.
- **Syndication:** became the **worldwide digital and satellite distribution partner** for the Malayalam action thriller *Kattlan*.
- **B2B syndication deals deferred** on geopolitical uncertainty — the direct cause of the 17% digital decline, and by nature deferred rather than lost.
- **Awards:** first AI-powered campaign *Kindness Badhaye Goodness* won the Baby Blue Elephant at Kyoorius Creative Awards 2026 and a bronze at Good Ads Matter.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Digital (₹56cr, −17%)** splits into a **lumpy B2B syndication/licensing leg** (the decline) and a **growing consumer leg** (fresh content, stronger engagement, improved ad monetisation). Management insists there is **no under-utilisation of the library** — 9bn views a quarter is the proof — and that titles like *Welcome*, *Jab We Met*, *Phir Hera Pheri* are consistent performers wherever placed.
- **Traditional (₹76cr, +5%)**: FTA/free-dish channels are **100% advertising-monetised**; some channels are not at break-even because the ad market has been persistently subdued. Investment here is being "pared down significantly," with possible channel rationalisation not ruled out ("whether it is in terms of channel scale rationalization or whatever, that will come to know as we go ahead").
- **ShemarooMe (SVoD, Gujarati-led)**: described as holding a "pole position" and effectively the **default Gujarati entertainment platform**. Uniquely offers a **two-year subscription plan** with decent uptake — management reads this as a trust signal, since consumers pay two years ahead without content visibility. **No numbers disclosed** — the COO would say only "strong double-digit revenue growth trajectory."
- **FAST channels**: the global FAST ecosystem has been **de-growing for 12–18 months**; Shemaroo has cut back from more channels to **two**, and treats it as experimental — "if it scales, we will scale up… if it doesn't scale, we will scale back."
- **Connected TV** is the stated strategic focus within YouTube — long-form content on CTV monetises significantly better than views elsewhere, and management says YouTube itself is focusing there.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Connected TV / long-form on YouTube** — the explicit monetisation priority; "more than views… your revenue per view or monetisation metrics are far more important."
- **ShemarooMe Gujarati** — deepening lifetime value through content cadence and renewals rather than paid acquisition.
- **Micro-dramas / short-form**: technologically ready on the back end, some experimental investment, but **deliberately not pressing the pedal** because monetisation remains "a bit of a question mark." Explosive consumption growth in China and now India acknowledged.
- **YouTube Shorts**: content has been repurposed into Shorts, but **monetisation "has nearly not moved"** — an expected July policy update had not materialised as of the call.
- **AI** — first AI-powered campaign won two industry awards; AI investment is grouped within the digital-first redirection.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **A fully charged-off legacy library is a structurally high-margin asset**: content already paid for and amortised carries **80–90% margins** wherever monetised, versus roughly zero-to-negative on freshly acquired content bought at competitive prices. This is the single most important economic fact of the business, and management stated it twice.
- **Library travels well digitally** — 9bn quarterly views and consistent performance of catalogue titles across platforms give what the CEO calls "a very good futuristic predictability of the revenue."
- **ShemarooMe's Gujarati position**: default-platform status plus a two-year prepaid plan that no other Indian platform offers, evidencing brand trust and locking in duration.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Margin is explicitly **not a linear function of revenue**. Three drivers: (i) **mix** — mine more of the already-charged-off legacy library, which carries the highest incremental EBITDA; (ii) **cost** — a significant operational-efficiency drive over the last 2–3 quarters, whose effect should show quarter-on-quarter; (iii) **value-chain position** — consumer-facing OTT makes no money for anyone today; aggregation/licensing of owned content is the profitable middle; content creation/production-for-hire is a fixed **10–20%** margin business.
- **Blended digital margin depends on legacy vs newly-acquired mix**, not on the platform (YouTube vs syndication) — management corrected an analyst who assumed YouTube was structurally the highest-margin channel.
- The historical **±30% margin oscillation** was largely the accelerated charge-off; the new steady state is a genuinely different, digital-weighted structure and management would not commit to a number this year.
- Two large ShemarooMe cost buckets: **customer acquisition (ATL + performance marketing)** and **content** — profitability comes from shifting the base toward renewals, where CAC does not apply.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- **Content investment is now the capex**, and it is being redirected: new content creation in traditional has been **scaled down "a lot"**; acquisition/creation in digital is being **dialled up**. The >50% cut in traditional new-initiative spend is "well on track."
- ShemarooMe required **no significant upfront CAPEX** — the Gujarati position was the "right to win" at the starting point; ongoing spend is **OPEX in nature** (continuous tech integrations, payment gateways, features, customer service) plus content.
- The **OHO Gujarati catalogue** (April 2026) is the quarter's main content acquisition.
capital allocation:
- **Debt ₹311cr against inventory ₹348cr.** A debt-reduction plan exists for FY27; management refused to size it, citing geopolitical uncertainty and the BARC blackout — "it's no point that I give you a target or a number right now and then it doesn't hold by the end of the year."
- Capital is being **reallocated from traditional to digital across every dimension** — money, people, AI work, content creation.
- Explicit growth-versus-burn discipline on ShemarooMe: "it's very easy for me to scale up by burning significantly more amount of money… but then that will burn a big hole on our cash flow and balance sheet… few quarters later we would ourselves scratch our heads."
risks & watch-items:
1. **BARC ratings blackout** — began ~a month before the call, hits traditional ad monetisation directly and TV-linked syndication indirectly. No visibility on resolution. Compounds an already subdued ad market.
2. **Digital revenue is lumpy** — a 17% decline driven by deferred B2B syndication. Deferrals are recoverable in principle, but the timing is not in Shemaroo's control.
3. **Debt at ₹311cr with ~₹30cr+ of annual interest** against a business at roughly break-even EBITDA — the reduction plan is unquantified.
4. **Traditional TV is structurally declining** and some FTA channels are below break-even; channel rationalisation is possible but unconfirmed.
5. **ShemarooMe is ~2 years from profitability** and completely undisclosed — no revenue, subscribers, ARPU, DAU/MAU. An analyst explicitly requested more granularity; management committed only to discuss it offline.
6. **YouTube Shorts monetisation has not moved**, and an expected July policy update had not landed. Micro-drama monetisation is likewise unresolved.
7. **FAST is globally de-growing** — Shemaroo has already cut from more channels to two.
8. **Digital growth has been only 9–10% CAGR FY24→FY26**, below the +20% an analyst argued should be achievable; management's defence is industry growth was itself low and that it will not buy growth at the cost of cash.
management quality / tone: Measured, technically candid, and unusually willing to correct analysts' mental models — the CEO and COO both pushed back on the assumption that YouTube is inherently the highest-margin channel, explaining that margin follows **content vintage**, not platform. They also volunteered that FAST is de-growing globally and that Shorts/micro-drama monetisation remains unproven, rather than riding the narrative. The commitments they did make were specific and falsifiable (EBITDA-positive this year, bottom-line positive next year, >50% cut in traditional new-initiative spend). The weakness is disclosure: an analyst told them directly that "there are too many things which are not disclosed and hence very difficult to figure out… how the business is moving," and the honest answer was a commitment to discuss offline. The refusal to size the debt-reduction plan is defensible given the BARC blackout, but it leaves the balance-sheet trajectory unmodellable.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The margin driver is content vintage, not platform.** Fully charged-off legacy content yields **80–90%** margins on any platform; newly acquired content can be zero or negative because acquisition is competitively priced. This single insight reframes the whole P&L — Shemaroo's earnings power is a function of how hard it mines the paid-for library relative to how much new content it buys.
- **Views are the wrong YouTube metric.** Total views are flat/range-bound and management is deliberately steering to **connected TV long-form**, which monetises far better per view. "Finally, your revenue per view or monetisation metrics are far more important."
- **The ₹18cr ex-initiative EBITDA is the real run-rate signal** — the reported −₹2cr is masked by ₹20cr of deliberate, and now shrinking (on the traditional side), investment.
- **The two-year ShemarooMe subscription plan is a genuinely unusual asset** — no other Indian platform offers one. It is prepaid duration and a trust signal in a category where churn is the killer.
- **The negative-margin history was an accounting programme, not operations.** With charge-off normalised and inventory at ₹348cr, prior-period margins are not a valid base for forecasting.
- **Micro-drama and Shorts are being held deliberately**: the tech is ready, the content isn't bought. This is a real, low-cost option that gets exercised only when monetisation proves out.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Digital (₹56cr, −17%)** splits into a **lumpy B2B syndication/licensing leg** (the decline) and a **growing consumer leg** (fresh content, stronger engagement, improved ad monetisation). Management insists there is **no under-utilisation of the library** — 9bn views a quarter is the proof — and that titles like *Welcome*, *Jab We Met*, *Phir Hera Pheri* are consistent performers wherever placed.
- **Traditional (₹76cr, +5%)**: FTA/free-dish channels are **100% advertising-monetised**; some channels are not at break-even because the ad market has been persistently subdued. Investment here is being "pared down significantly," with possible channel rationalisation not ruled out ("whether it is in terms of channel scale rationalization or whatever, that will come to know as we go ahead").
- **ShemarooMe (SVoD, Gujarati-led)**: described as holding a "pole position" and effectively the **default Gujarati entertainment platform**. Uniquely offers a **two-year subscription plan** with decent uptake — management reads this as a trust signal, since consumers pay two years ahead without content visibility. **No numbers disclosed** — the COO would say only "strong double-digit revenue growth trajectory."
- **FAST channels**: the global FAST ecosystem has been **de-growing for 12–18 months**; Shemaroo has cut back from more channels to **two**, and treats it as experimental — "if it scales, we will scale up… if it doesn't scale, we will scale back."

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue growth: "healthy double-digit" blended, over the next 2–3 years** — built as digital growing at a low-double-digit industry rate **plus at least a couple of percentage points** of outperformance, with **traditional flat (explicitly "not a degrowth")**.
- **Profitability: "the aim will be for the year to be EBITDA positive at least"** and **"we are very confident that next year we will be bottom-line positive also."** Quarter-on-quarter improvement expected every quarter.
- **Margin: "upwards of 20% EBITDA is something that we should aim for"** on a 2–3 year view (aspiration, hedged — "I don't know whether we will be able to achieve that or not").
- **Debt: a reduction plan exists for this year**, but **no quantum given** — explicitly withheld because of geopolitical uncertainty and the BARC blackout. Expect quarterly ups and downs.
- **New-initiative spend on traditional media: >50% reduction in FY27 vs FY26 — "we are well on track."**
- **H2 expected to be materially stronger** — festive season, operational gains, and the digital consumption engine.
- **Advertising outlook for traditional business: expected to remain subdued in the near term** (BARC blackout + macro + geopolitics).
- **ShemarooMe path to profitability: "at least about two years away"** — dependent on building a large permanent subscriber base and minimising churn.
- **No further inventory write-down risk** — "now we are in a normal charge-off cycle."
- Explicitly **declined**: any ShemarooMe revenue/subscriber/DAU/MAU/ARPU disclosure; a revenue threshold for sustained positive EBITDA; a segment revenue split target for FY27 beyond the directional double-digit/flat framing.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Connected TV / long-form on YouTube** — the explicit monetisation priority; "more than views… your revenue per view or monetisation metrics are far more important."
- **ShemarooMe Gujarati** — deepening lifetime value through content cadence and renewals rather than paid acquisition.
- **Micro-dramas / short-form**: technologically ready on the back end, some experimental investment, but **deliberately not pressing the pedal** because monetisation remains "a bit of a question mark." Explosive consumption growth in China and now India acknowledged.
- **YouTube Shorts**: content has been repurposed into Shorts, but **monetisation "has nearly not moved"** — an expected July policy update had not materialised as of the call.
- **AI** — first AI-powered campaign won two industry awards; AI investment is grouped within the digital-first redirection.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Digital media industry (India) projected to grow from INR 1.11 trillion (2025) to INR 1.3 trillion in 2026 (17% YoY) and INR 1.64 trillion by 2028 (14% CAGR), driven by 5G rollout, Connected TV scaling and a maturing e-commerce advertising ecosystem.
- A substantial part of the Company's digital revenue now originates from Connected TV platforms, reflecting evolving consumer viewing habits and positioning the Company to benefit from growing demand for premium digital content and higher-value advertising inventory.
- Television/broadcasting industry faces structural headwinds — Pay TV lost 11.5 million households industry-wide in 2025 and linear TV advertising revenue is projected to decline at a CAGR of -4.6% through 2028 — as high-value households and advertisers migrate to digital and Connected TV.
- Regional-language content demand is rising — regional language content now accounts for 56% of all digital content produced (up from 48% in 2024) — supporting the Company's regional-content investment strategy (Gujarati, South Indian).
- Emergence of the 'micro-drama' content segment (INR 6.5 billion industry revenue) signals a shift toward ultra-short, highly engaging scripted content as a new content format opportunity.
- Reduction in high-budget direct-to-OTT film acquisitions industry-wide, with platforms rationalising spend toward profitability and intensifying focus on hyper-local, regional-language programming.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- Margin is explicitly **not a linear function of revenue**. Three drivers: (i) **mix** — mine more of the already-charged-off legacy library, which carries the highest incremental EBITDA; (ii) **cost** — a significant operational-efficiency drive over the last 2–3 quarters, whose effect should show quarter-on-quarter; (iii) **value-chain position** — consumer-facing OTT makes no money for anyone today; aggregation/licensing of owned content is the profitable middle; content creation/production-for-hire is a fixed **10–20%** margin business.
- **Blended digital margin depends on legacy vs newly-acquired mix**, not on the platform (YouTube vs syndication) — management corrected an analyst who assumed YouTube was structurally the highest-margin channel.
- The historical **±30% margin oscillation** was largely the accelerated charge-off; the new steady state is a genuinely different, digital-weighted structure and management would not commit to a number this year.
- Two large ShemarooMe cost buckets: **customer acquisition (ATL + performance marketing)** and **content** — profitability comes from shifting the base toward renewals, where CAC does not apply.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- **Debt ₹311cr against inventory ₹348cr.** A debt-reduction plan exists for FY27; management refused to size it, citing geopolitical uncertainty and the BARC blackout — "it's no point that I give you a target or a number right now and then it doesn't hold by the end of the year."
- Capital is being **reallocated from traditional to digital across every dimension** — money, people, AI work, content creation.
- Explicit growth-versus-burn discipline on ShemarooMe: "it's very easy for me to scale up by burning significantly more amount of money… but then that will burn a big hole on our cash flow and balance sheet… few quarters later we would ourselves scratch our heads."

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: As an asset-light content/media business, Shemaroo's 'expansion' during FY26 took the form of content-library and platform investments rather than physical capacity: it acquired the OHO Gujarati content library (adding 22+ web series) to strengthen ShemarooMe's Gujarati leadership; launched the 'Shemaroo Premiere' banner with its first Hindi original web series, broadening the platform beyond regional content; took its first steps into international co-production via a partnership with Globalsphere Studios for a Turkish drama series; expanded investment/syndication in South Indian (Malayalam) film titles; and realigned its broadcasting channel portfolio by relaunching Chumbak TV as Shemaroo Josh (adding premium Hindi movies to its youth-focused programming) to support viewership recovery.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Measured, technically candid, and unusually willing to correct analysts' mental models — the CEO and COO both pushed back on the assumption that YouTube is inherently the highest-margin channel, explaining that margin follows **content vintage**, not platform. They also volunteered that FAST is de-growing globally and that Shorts/micro-drama monetisation remains unproven, rather than riding the narrative. The commitments they did make were specific and falsifiable (EBITDA-positive this year, bottom-line positive next year, >50% cut in traditional new-initiative spend). The weakness is disclosure: an analyst told them directly that "there are too many things which are not disclosed and hence very difficult to figure out… how the business is moving," and the honest answer was a commitment to discuss offline. The refusal to size the debt-reduction plan is defensible given the BARC blackout, but it leaves the balance-sheet trajectory unmodellable.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Extensive owned content library (3 billion+ hours, 10,000+ titles) spanning multiple languages and genres, built over 60+ years
- One of the largest digital content networks in India — 100+ YouTube channels with 300 million+ monthly active viewerbase and 100 million+ daily views; flagship channels Shemaroo Filmi Gaane (74 million subscribers) and Shemaroo Entertainment (61 million subscribers)
- Deep, longstanding syndication relationships with leading broadcasters (Zee, Sony, JioStar) and digital platforms (Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, JioHotstar, Sony LIV)
- Brand built over 60 years with strong management team of experienced industry professionals
- Multi-platform distribution ecosystem spanning traditional (TV syndication, DTH, in-flight) and digital (OTT, AVOD/SVOD) channels

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
1. **BARC ratings blackout** — began ~a month before the call, hits traditional ad monetisation directly and TV-linked syndication indirectly. No visibility on resolution. Compounds an already subdued ad market.
2. **Digital revenue is lumpy** — a 17% decline driven by deferred B2B syndication. Deferrals are recoverable in principle, but the timing is not in Shemaroo's control.
3. **Debt at ₹311cr with ~₹30cr+ of annual interest** against a business at roughly break-even EBITDA — the reduction plan is unquantified.
4. **Traditional TV is structurally declining** and some FTA channels are below break-even; channel rationalisation is possible but unconfirmed.
5. **ShemarooMe is ~2 years from profitability** and completely undisclosed — no revenue, subscribers, ARPU, DAU/MAU. An analyst explicitly requested more granularity; management committed only to discuss it offline.
6. **YouTube Shorts monetisation has not moved**, and an expected July policy update had not landed. Micro-drama monetisation is likewise unresolved.
7. **FAST is globally de-growing** — Shemaroo has already cut from more channels to two.
8. **Digital growth has been only 9–10% CAGR FY24→FY26**, below the +20% an analyst argued should be achievable; management's defence is industry growth was itself low and that it will not buy growth at the cost of cash.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **The margin driver is content vintage, not platform.** Fully charged-off legacy content yields **80–90%** margins on any platform; newly acquired content can be zero or negative because acquisition is competitively priced. This single insight reframes the whole P&L — Shemaroo's earnings power is a function of how hard it mines the paid-for library relative to how much new content it buys.
- **Views are the wrong YouTube metric.** Total views are flat/range-bound and management is deliberately steering to **connected TV long-form**, which monetises far better per view. "Finally, your revenue per view or monetisation metrics are far more important."
- **The ₹18cr ex-initiative EBITDA is the real run-rate signal** — the reported −₹2cr is masked by ₹20cr of deliberate, and now shrinking (on the traditional side), investment.
- **The two-year ShemarooMe subscription plan is a genuinely unusual asset** — no other Indian platform offers one. It is prepaid duration and a trust signal in a category where churn is the killer.
- **The negative-margin history was an accounting programme, not operations.** With charge-off normalised and inventory at ₹348cr, prior-period margins are not a valid base for forecasting.
- **Micro-drama and Shorts are being held deliberately**: the tech is ready, the content isn't bought. This is a real, low-cost option that gets exercised only when monetisation proves out.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Digital forms a significant pillar of the growth strategy — across advertising-supported platforms, subscription services and content licensing, the Company aims to expand audience reach, deepen engagement and unlock new monetisation opportunities.
- Traditional media businesses are managed with discipline, to continue extending the reach and value of content assets even as the segment faces industry-wide pressure.
- Journey from content aggregation towards content creation — evidenced by the launch of the 'Shemaroo Premiere' banner and the platform's first Hindi original web series.

Management insists there is **no under-utilisation of the library** — 9bn views a quarter is the proof — and that titles like *Welcome*, *Jab We Met*, *Phir Hera Pheri* are consistent performers wherever placed.
- **Traditional (₹76cr, +5%)**: FTA/free-dish channels are **100% advertising-monetised**; some channels are not at break-even because the ad market has been persistently subdued. Investment here is being "pared down significantly," with possible channel rationalisation not ruled out ("whether it is in terms of channel scale rationalization or whatever, that will come to know as we go ahead").
- **ShemarooMe (SVoD, Gujarati-led)**: described as holding a "pole position" and effectively the **default Gujarati entertainment platform**. Uniquely offers a **two-year subscription plan** with decent uptake — management reads this as a trust signal, since consumers pay two years ahead without content visibility. **No numbers disclosed** — the COO would say only "strong double-digit revenue growth trajectory."
- **FAST channels**: the global FAST ecosystem has been **de-growing for 12–18 months**; Shemaroo has cut back from more channels to **two**, and treats it as experimental — "if it scales, we will scale up… if it doesn't scale, we will scale back."
- **Connected TV** is the stated strategic focus within YouTube — long-form content on CTV monetises significantly better than views elsewhere, and management says YouTube itself is focusing there.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Connected TV / long-form on YouTube** — the explicit monetisation priority; "more than views… your revenue per view or monetisation metrics are far more important."
- **ShemarooMe Gujarati** — deepening lifetime value through content cadence and renewals rather than paid acquisition.
- **Micro-dramas / short-form**: technologically ready on the back end, some experimental investment, but **deliberately not pressing the pedal** because monetisation remains "a bit of a question mark." Explosive consumption growth in China and now India acknowledged.
- **YouTube Shorts**: content has been repurposed into Shorts, but **monetisation "has nearly not moved"** — an expected July policy update had not materialised as of the call.
- **AI** — first AI-powered campaign won two industry awards; AI investment is grouped within the digital-first redirection.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **A fully charged-off legacy library is a structurally high-margin asset**: content already paid for and amortised carries **80–90% margins** wherever monetised, versus roughly zero-to-negative on freshly acquired content bought at competitive prices. This is the single most important economic fact of the business, and management stated it twice.
- **Library travels well digitally** — 9bn quarterly views and consistent performance of catalogue titles across platforms give what the CEO calls "a very good futuristic predictability of the revenue."
- **ShemarooMe's Gujarati position**: default-platform status plus a two-year prepaid plan that no other Indian platform offers, evidencing brand trust and locking in duration.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Margin is explicitly **not a linear function of revenue**. Three drivers: (i) **mix** — mine more of the already-charged-off legacy library, which carries the highest incremental EBITDA; (ii) **cost** — a significant operational-efficiency drive over the last 2–3 quarters, whose effect should show quarter-on-quarter; (iii) **value-chain position** — consumer-facing OTT makes no money for anyone today; aggregation/licensing of owned content is the profitable middle; content creation/production-for-hire is a fixed **10–20%** margin business.
- **Blended digital margin depends on legacy vs newly-acquired mix**, not on the platform (YouTube vs syndication) — management corrected an analyst who assumed YouTube was structurally the highest-margin channel.
- The historical **±30% margin oscillation** was largely the accelerated charge-off; the new steady state is a genuinely different, digital-weighted structure and management would not commit to a number this year.
- Two large ShemarooMe cost buckets: **customer acquisition (ATL + performance marketing)** and **content** — profitability comes from shifting the base toward renewals, where CAC does not apply.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- **Content investment is now the capex**, and it is being redirected: new content creation in traditional has been **scaled down "a lot"**; acquisition/creation in digital is being **dialled up**. The >50% cut in traditional new-initiative spend is "well on track."
- ShemarooMe required **no significant upfront CAPEX** — the Gujarati position was the "right to win" at the starting point; ongoing spend is **OPEX in nature** (continuous tech integrations, payment gateways, features, customer service) plus content.
- The **OHO Gujarati catalogue** (April 2026) is the quarter's main content acquisition.
capital allocation:
- **Debt ₹311cr against inventory ₹348cr.** A debt-reduction plan exists for FY27; management refused to size it, citing geopolitical uncertainty and the BARC blackout — "it's no point that I give you a target or a number right now and then it doesn't hold by the end of the year."
- Capital is being **reallocated from traditional to digital across every dimension** — money, people, AI work, content creation.
- Explicit growth-versus-burn discipline on ShemarooMe: "it's very easy for me to scale up by burning significantly more amount of money… but then that will burn a big hole on our cash flow and balance sheet… few quarters later we would ourselves scratch our heads."
risks & watch-items:
1. **BARC ratings blackout** — began ~a month before the call, hits traditional ad monetisation directly and TV-linked syndication indirectly. No visibility on resolution. Compounds an already subdued ad market.
2. **Digital revenue is lumpy** — a 17% decline driven by deferred B2B syndication. Deferrals are recoverable in principle, but the timing is not in Shemaroo's control.
3. **Debt at ₹311cr with ~₹30cr+ of annual interest** against a business at roughly break-even EBITDA — the reduction plan is unquantified.
4. **Traditional TV is structurally declining** and some FTA channels are below break-even; channel rationalisation is possible but unconfirmed.
5. **ShemarooMe is ~2 years from profitability** and completely undisclosed — no revenue, subscribers, ARPU, DAU/MAU. An analyst explicitly requested more granularity; management committed only to discuss it offline.
6. **YouTube Shorts monetisation has not moved**, and an expected July policy update had not landed. Micro-drama monetisation is likewise unresolved.
7. **FAST is globally de-growing** — Shemaroo has already cut from more channels to two.
8. **Digital growth has been only 9–10% CAGR FY24→FY26**, below the +20% an analyst argued should be achievable; management's defence is industry growth was itself low and that it will not buy growth at the cost of cash.
management quality / tone: Measured, technically candid, and unusually willing to correct analysts' mental models — the CEO and COO both pushed back on the assumption that YouTube is inherently the highest-margin channel, explaining that margin follows **content vintage**, not platform. They also volunteered that FAST is de-growing globally and that Shorts/micro-drama monetisation remains unproven, rather than riding the narrative. The commitments they did make were specific and falsifiable (EBITDA-positive this year, bottom-line positive next year, >50% cut in traditional new-initiative spend). The weakness is disclosure: an analyst told them directly that "there are too many things which are not disclosed and hence very difficult to figure out… how the business is moving," and the honest answer was a commitment to discuss offline. The refusal to size the debt-reduction plan is defensible given the BARC blackout, but it leaves the balance-sheet trajectory unmodellable.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The margin driver is content vintage, not platform.** Fully charged-off legacy content yields **80–90%** margins on any platform; newly acquired content can be zero or negative because acquisition is competitively priced. This single insight reframes the whole P&L — Shemaroo's earnings power is a function of how hard it mines the paid-for library relative to how much new content it buys.
- **Views are the wrong YouTube metric.** Total views are flat/range-bound and management is deliberately steering to **connected TV long-form**, which monetises far better per view. "Finally, your revenue per view or monetisation metrics are far more important."
- **The ₹18cr ex-initiative EBITDA is the real run-rate signal** — the reported −₹2cr is masked by ₹20cr of deliberate, and now shrinking (on the traditional side), investment.
- **The two-year ShemarooMe subscription plan is a genuinely unusual asset** — no other Indian platform offers one. It is prepaid duration and a trust signal in a category where churn is the killer.
- **The negative-margin history was an accounting programme, not operations.** With charge-off normalised and inventory at ₹348cr, prior-period margins are not a valid base for forecasting.
- **Micro-drama and Shorts are being held deliberately**: the tech is ready, the content isn't bought. This is a real, low-cost option that gets exercised only when monetisation proves out.
